**Use the table for questions 1–2.** Car rental branches, July. *Utilisation = % of car-days on which a car was rented.*

| Branch | Cars | Utilisation | Daily rate (€) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Airport | 150 | 90% | 55 |
| Centre | 80 | 75% | 48 |
| Station | 60 | 80% | 50 |
| Harbour | 40 | 70% | 62 |

questions.stem: Which branch earns the lowest revenue per car per day (across all its cars, rented or not)?
options: Airport
Centre
Station
Harbour
Station and Harbour equally
questions.explain: Utilisation × rate: Airport €49.50, Centre €36.00, Station €40.00, Harbour €43.40.

questions.stem: What was the Station branch's total rental revenue in July (31 days)?
A mobile plan costs €15 a month and includes 10 GB. Extra data costs €2 per GB or part of a GB. 21% VAT is added to the total. What is the bill for a month with 13.4 GB used?
questions.explain: 3.4 GB extra is charged as 4 GB = €8. (15 + 8) × 1.21 = €27.83. €26.38 charges exactly 3.4 GB; €26.15 adds VAT to the base fee only.

questions.stem: What number comes next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
What was Brand X's share of the two brands' combined sales in 2025?
By what percentage did Brand X's sales grow between 2022 and 2025?
questions.explain: (70 − 40)/40 = 75%. 42.9% divides by the final value.

questions.stem: In 2026, Brand Y's sales grow by 10% and Brand X's sales grow by the same number of units as between 2024 and 2025. Which brand sells more in 2026, and by how much?
options: Brand X, by 200 units
Brand Y, by 200 units
Brand Y, by 2,000 units
Brand X, by 7,000 units
They sell the same

questions.stem: A salesperson earns 3% commission on the first €40,000 of monthly sales and 5% on sales above that, plus a €500 bonus if monthly sales exceed €100,000. What does she earn on sales of €104,000?
Each row follows the same rule. Row 1: 8, 2, 20. Row 2: 6, 3, 18. Row 3: 10, 5, ?
A website had 1.98 million visits in a year. 2.1% of visits ended in an order, and the average order was €49.50. Which is the best estimate of the year's online sales?
A price rises by 25% and then falls by 20%. What is the overall change?
A project needs 480 hours of work. Four consultants each work 8 hours a day but spend 25% of their time on other tasks. How many working days will the project take?
questions.explain: Productive hours per day = 4 × 8 × 0.75 = 24 → 480/24 = 20 days. 15 ignores the 25%.

two.md: **Questions 13–14.** For each pair of statements, choose the option that best describes their relationship.

questions.stem:
All drivers in the fleet hold a forklift licence. No one under 21 holds a forklift licence.

**Conclusion:** No driver in the fleet is under 21.
options: The conclusion follows
The conclusion does not follow
questions.explain: Driver → licence → not under 21. It follows.

questions.stem:
Some managers are engineers. Some engineers work remotely.

**Conclusion:** Some managers work remotely.
options: The conclusion follows
The conclusion does not follow
questions.explain: Two chained "some" statements give no conclusion: the remote engineers may not be managers.

questions.stem:
Only products that pass quality control are shipped. All products made on Line 3 last week were shipped.

Which statement must be true?
options: All products that passed quality control were made on Line 3.
No products from other lines were shipped last week.
Line 3 never fails quality control.
All products made on Line 3 last week passed quality control.
Some products that passed quality control were not shipped.
questions.explain: "Only": being shipped requires passing quality control. A reverses the relationship; C generalises to every week.

questions.stem:
No one in the legal team uses the old software. Everyone in the Lisbon office uses the old software. Marta works in the Lisbon office.

Which statement must be true?
options: Marta uses the new software.
Marta is not in the legal team.
All users of the old software work in Lisbon.
Some legal team members work in Lisbon.
Marta will move to the legal team.
questions.explain: Marta uses the old software, so she can't be in legal. A doesn't follow: she may use both.

questions.stem:
Five boxes (Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, White) are stacked in positions 1 (bottom) to 5 (top).
- White is at the top or the bottom.
- Green is directly above Red.
- Blue is above Yellow.
- Neither Red nor Yellow is at the bottom.
- Green is not at the top.
- Blue is not next to Green.

Which box is in position 3?
options: Red
Blue
Green
Yellow
White
questions.explain: Red and Yellow can't be at the bottom (rule), nor can Green or Blue (each has a box below it), so White = 1. If Red–Green were 3–4, Blue would end up in 5 next to Green. So Red 2, Green 3, Yellow 4, Blue 5.

questions.stem:
Five candidates (Ana, Ben, Carla, Dev, Eva) are interviewed at 9:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00.
- Eva is interviewed at 11:00.
- Dev is interviewed immediately after Ana.
- Ana is not interviewed at 9:00.
- Ben is interviewed before Carla.

Who is interviewed at 10:00?
options: Ana
Ben
Carla
Dev
Eva
questions.explain: Ana–Dev don't fit at 9–10 or 10–11 (Eva is at 11), so they are 12–13. Ben 9:00 and Carla 10:00.

questions.stem:
Four colleagues (Ann, Bo, Cy, Di) each prefer a different drink: coffee, tea, juice or water.
- Ann drinks neither coffee nor tea.
- Bo drinks juice.
- Cy does not drink coffee.

Who drinks coffee?
options: Ann
Bo
Cy
Di
questions.explain: Bo juice → Ann water → Cy tea → Di coffee.

questions.stem:
"In a survey on our website, 85% of respondents said they were satisfied with our delivery times. So most of our customers are satisfied with delivery."

Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: Competitors have slower deliveries.
Delivery times have improved this year.
Customers value delivery time above price.
The people who answered the website survey are representative of all customers.
The survey had more than 1,000 responses.
questions.explain: If the people answering on the website don't represent all customers, the 85% can't be extended to them.

questions.stem:
"Branches that use the new scheduling software have 20% lower overtime costs than branches that don't. The software therefore cuts overtime."

Which statement, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the normal rate.
The software is easy to learn.
Staff in all branches work similar contracts.
The software was installed only in branches that had already shortened their opening hours.
Some branches plan to install it next year.
questions.explain: The difference may come from the shorter hours, not the software.

questions.stem:
A school says its new reading programme raised pupils' reading scores.

Which statement, if true, most strengthens the claim?
options: Reading scores rose across the country this year.
Pupils in the programme improved by 12 points, while a comparable group taught in the usual way at the same school improved by 3 points over the same period.
Teachers received two days of training.
The programme uses new books.
Parents like the new programme.
questions.explain: A comparable group over the same period isolates the programme's effect.

questions.stem:
In a tournament, every team plays every other team exactly once. A total of 15 matches were played.

How many teams took part?

All of the firm's 2025 projects were in either retail or energy. Every energy project was led by a partner from the Madrid office. None of the retail projects lasted more than six months. Project Orion, a 2025 project, lasted nine months.

Which statement must be true?
options: Orion was led by a partner from the Madrid office.
Orion was a retail project.
All energy projects lasted more than six months.
Orion was the firm's longest project.
Every Madrid partner led an energy project.
questions.explain: Nine months → not retail → energy → led by a Madrid partner.

questions.stem:
(1) The company's share price fell 15% in one day.
(2) The company announced that its CEO had resigned unexpectedly.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are independent causes.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: The resignation (2) causes the fall (1).

questions.stem:
(1) A local bakery's bread sales fell this week.
(2) Car insurance premiums rose nationally this week.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are independent causes.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: Unrelated: effects of independent causes.

questions.stem:
A firm invites applicants to interview if **either**:
- they have a degree in economics, business or engineering **and** at least 2 years of work experience; **or**
- they have a master's degree in any field **and** at least 1 year of work experience.

Which applicant is invited?
options: Engineering degree, 18 months' experience, no master's.
Business degree and a master's, 6 months' experience.
Law degree, 5 years' experience, no master's.
History degree and a master's in history, 18 months' experience.
Economics degree, 1 year's experience, no master's.
questions.explain: D meets the second route (master's + at least 1 year). A and E don't reach 2 years; B doesn't reach 1 year; C has neither the degree nor a master's.

questions.stem:
Staff get a parking permit if they live more than 10 km from the office or hold a disability badge. Staff who joined less than 6 months ago are not eligible unless they hold a disability badge.

An employee joined 4 months ago, lives 25 km away and has no disability badge. Is she eligible?
options: Yes, because she lives more than 10 km away.
No, because she joined less than 6 months ago.
Yes, because new staff need extra support.
No, because she lives too far away.
It cannot be determined.
questions.explain: The tenure exclusion can only be overridden by a disability badge.

questions.stem: Which statements can be concluded from the chart? **Select all that apply.**
options: North Hospital's waiting time fell every month.
South Hospital's waiting time rose every month.
South Hospital's waiting time first exceeded North's in May.
In June, the gap between the two hospitals was 14 minutes.
South Hospital's waiting time will exceed 100 minutes in August.
questions.explain: A ✗ it rises in April. B ✔. C ✔ April 86 < 92, May 90 > 85. D ✔ 94 − 80. E ✗ forecast.

questions.stem:
Online shop, first quarter:

| Category | Orders | Returns | Average order (€) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shoes | 1,200 | 240 | 60 |
| Clothing | 2,000 | 300 | 40 |
| Accessories | 800 | 40 | 25 |

Which statements can be concluded from the data? **Select all that apply.**
options: Shoes have the highest return rate.
Clothing had the most returns.
The return rate across all orders was 13.3%.
Clothing generated the highest total order value.
Accessories customers are the most satisfied.
questions.explain: Return rates 20%, 15%, 5%. A ✔. B ✔ 300. C ✗ 580/4,000 = 14.5% (13.3% is the simple average). D ✔ €80,000 vs 72,000 and 20,000. E ✗ cannot be known.

chart.title: Electricity use by source
chart.note: Total electricity use: 500 MWh in 2024, 600 MWh in 2025.

questions.stem: By how much did electricity from solar increase between 2024 and 2025?
options: 100 MWh
180 MWh
80 MWh
50 MWh
10 MWh
questions.explain: 0.20 × 500 = 100 → 0.30 × 600 = 180 MWh: +80. 10 is the change in percentage points.

questions.stem:
Customer survey: "Would you recommend us?"

| Region | Yes | No | Unsure | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| North | 120 | 30 | 50 | 200 |
| East | 90 | 45 | 15 | 150 |
| South | 140 | 25 | 35 | 200 |

What percentage of all respondents who answered "No" are from the East?
questions.explain: Total "No" = 100 → 45/100 = 45%. 30% is 45/150 (the "No" share within the East).

questions.stem: A product is rated by three groups: 50 customers give an average of 4.2, 30 customers an average of 3.8 and 20 customers an average of 2.9. What is the overall average rating?
questions.explain: (210 + 114 + 58)/100 = 3.82. 3.63 is the simple average of the three averages.

questions.stem: Salaries (€k) of six staff: 28, 31, 35, 40, 44, 90. What are the median and the mean?
options: Median 35, mean 44.7
Median 37.5, mean 37.5
Median 37.5, mean 53.6
Median 40, mean 44.7
Median 37.5, mean 44.7

questions.stem: Across 50 stores, the correlation between hours of staff training and sales is 0.8. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Training causes higher sales.
80% of sales are explained by training.
There is a strong negative relationship.
There is a strong positive association, but it does not show that training causes higher sales.
There is no relationship between training and sales.
questions.explain: A strong positive correlation, but no proof of causation (larger stores may both train more and sell more).

questions.stem: Two customer systems are being merged. One stores names as "Last, First" and the other as "First Last". What should you do before matching customers across them?
options: Delete customers whose names don't match.
Split names into separate first-name and last-name fields in both systems, then match.
Sort both lists alphabetically.
Keep only the larger system.
Match on the full name field as it is.
questions.explain: Standardise the structure before matching; otherwise no names will match.

questions.stem: In a sales spreadsheet, some amounts are stored as text (e.g. "1,250") and others as numbers. The SUM of the column is lower than expected. What is the best fix?
options: Convert the text values to numbers (removing the thousands separator) and check that every value is numeric.
Retype the total by hand.
Delete the rows stored as text.
Use AVERAGE instead of SUM.
Format the column as currency.
questions.explain: SUM ignores text. Changing the format (E) doesn't convert the contents.

questions.stem: A dataset has one row per transaction. To report the number of customers, an analyst counts the rows. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, each row is a customer.
The count should exclude the largest transactions.
Rows should be summed, not counted.
Customers with several transactions are counted more than once; the analyst should count distinct customer IDs.
The analyst should use the median.
questions.explain: Wrong level of detail: rows are transactions, not customers.

questions.stem: You want to show the relationship between advertising spend and sales across 50 stores. Which chart is most appropriate?
options: Scatter plot
Histogram of sales
Stacked bar chart
Line chart by store name
Pie chart
questions.explain: Relationship between two numerical variables → scatter plot.

questions.stem: A manager presents a chart of cumulative sign-ups since launch, which rises every month, and says: "Sign-ups are growing every month." What is the problem?
options: The chart should be a pie chart.
Cumulative charts cannot start at zero.
The chart has too many months.
A cumulative total rises whenever there are any sign-ups at all, even if monthly sign-ups are falling; monthly figures are needed.
There is no problem.
questions.explain: A cumulative total can only go up. To talk about growth, look at monthly sign-ups.
